metadata.title: Horizon 2026 — Broad Emerging Tech Landscape
metadata.description: Research-grounded mapping of 9 emerging technologies against the 10 TLCTC clusters. Placements are calibrated by mechanistic plausibility: a tech × cluster pair only appears if the technology directly changes the generic vulnerability exploited in that cluster. Quantum Computing, for example, is mapped only to #4/#5/#2 because its cryptanalytic capability does not alter the mechanism of flooding, malware execution, social engineering, or supply-chain trust acceptance.
metadata.author: TLCTC community (curated from public CTI reporting)

instances.notes: Generative models have commoditized phishing content, voice cloning, and deepfake video. Phishing-as-a-service offerings now bundle LLM-written lures with brand imitation; voice-cloning CEO fraud routinely observed. This is the dominant 'AI enables' scenario today.
instances.evidenceSource: Europol IOCTA 2024; NCSC NL 2024 annual report

instances.notes: Threat actors use LLMs to generate loaders, refactor existing malware families, and automate obfuscation routines. Microsoft and OpenAI publicly disclosed multiple state-actor accounts abusing hosted models for malware tooling.

references.title: Microsoft: Staying ahead of threat actors in the age of AI (2024)

instances.notes: LLMs accelerate exploit development from public CVE disclosures. Academic research (Kang et al.) showed frontier models can weaponize N-day vulnerabilities within hours. Relevant to client-side components (browsers, document readers) where attackers target the victim-side flaw.

references.title: Kang et al. — LLM agents can autonomously exploit one-day vulnerabilities (2024)

instances.evidenceSource: UIUC research 2024 on LLM exploit generation

instances.notes: Face-swap and synthetic video toolkits bypass remote identity verification (KYC) flows at exchanges, banks, and lenders. Several crypto exchanges and neo-banks reported sharp rises in deepfake-driven account-opening fraud.

Indirect prompt injection against RAG and assistant systems triggers unintended actions or exfiltrates context. Classified as #1 Abuse of Functions: the LLM input channel is used exactly as designed, but with adversarial payload content. Numerous public demonstrations against enterprise chatbots and Copilot-class tools.

references.title: Simon Willison — indirect prompt injection catalog

instances.notes: Agents wired to browser/shell/email tools can be coerced via indirect prompt injection to perform unintended tool calls (send emails, execute commands, modify files). Demonstrations against Anthropic computer-use, ChatGPT agents, and open-source frameworks. Still #1: the tool-use channel is being abused, not broken.

references.title: Simon Willison — 'agents are going to be hard'

instances.notes: Experimental agents run multi-turn chat with victims over Telegram/WhatsApp, dynamically adjusting persona and social-engineering pressure. Early adopters in pig-butchering and romance-scam operations; scale multiplier for criminal call-centers.

references.title: Interisle Consulting — GenAI and Scam Automation (2024)

instances.notes: Research agents chain recon → vulnerability discovery → exploitation autonomously (HackingBuddyGPT, XBOW). Dual-use: defensive red-team tooling is already being forked by offensive actors. First-mover level — not yet mass-deployed but publicly demonstrated against real targets.

Agents scan ecosystems for typo-squat opportunities, auto-generate malicious packages, and publish across npm/PyPI/RubyGems at a rate that outpaces human defenders. Early indicators in Shai-Hulud and Chalk/Debug incidents where tooling showed agent-like automation.

Agents chain infostealer output directly into authentication flows across harvested services, compressing the credential-theft → fraud timeline from hours to minutes. Collapses Axiom-X credential duality into a single automated pipeline.

A cryptographically relevant quantum computer would break RSA/ECC signing keys, enabling impersonation of any PKI identity (code-signing, TLS client certs, document signing). NIST PQC standards (FIPS 203/204/205) are the migration path; today this is latent.

Bulk interception of encrypted traffic today, retained for decryption once CRQC arrives. Threat is latent but real for long-lifetime secrets (state secrets, health records, IP). Drives urgency for PQC migration on confidential transport.

references.title: US OMB M-23-02 — Migrating to PQC

instances.notes: CRQC breaks server-side TLS authentication (as distinct from #4, which focuses on credential impersonation). Once asymmetric crypto is compromised, attackers can masquerade as the server itself and directly attack clients connecting to it.

Quantum magnetometers and gravimeters detect underground voids, shielded infrastructure, and electromagnetic signatures beyond classical sensor sensitivity. Implications for counter-intelligence and physical security around data centers, cable landings, and critical facilities.

Commercial drones and UGVs used for facility reconnaissance, payload delivery over fences, and close-approach RF sniffing. Established in conflict zones; 2023–2024 saw documented approaches to European data centers and substations.

Drones carrying pentest radios reach rooftop antennas and otherwise inaccessible Wi-Fi attack surfaces. IBM X-Force 'Fly, You Fools' demonstrated the pattern; real-world adoption still first-mover level.

Mirai-class botnets dominate volumetric DDoS. 2024–2025 Aisuru campaigns repeatedly set records above 6 Tbps; Cloudflare logged 5.6 Tbps events in October 2024. Commodity: the attack is offered as a paid service.

Routers, NAS, cameras, VPN gateways are preferred footholds. 2024–2025 saw active exploitation of ASUS, TP-Link, Fortinet, F5 BIG-IP by both state and criminal groups. Volt Typhoon's SOHO-router campaign is the canonical state-actor case.

Custom Linux/BSD/router firmware malware families (VPNFilter successors, Mirai variants) persist on edge devices. Difficult to detect without specialized telemetry; not growing rapidly in 2025 but remains steady as established technique.

Firmware-level backdoors delivered via compromised update channels or pre-installation implants. Referenced in US/UK advisories on specific vendor equipment. R-SUPPLY applies at the update trust-acceptance moment.

Hypothetical: implantable chips used for authentication (subdermal NFC/HID, payment implants) could be cloned via close-approach readers or surgically extracted. Not observed in the wild — watched by futures teams only.

Research has demonstrated wireless attacks on pacemakers and insulin pumps (Halperin 2008; Barnaby Jack historical). Not observed in the wild but classified as #8 because the attack crosses the human-physical boundary per R-ROLE.

Phishing inside VR/AR environments leverages social presence and bypasses traditional browser indicators. Incidents documented in Meta Horizon Worlds and VRChat 2023–2024. Still first-mover level — small but growing user base.

Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, Pico runtimes are complex client stacks (browser, media, passthrough) with growing attack surface. No mass exploitation observed; research papers have demonstrated sandbox escapes and side-channel gaze-tracking leaks.

The Ukraine/Russia conflict has normalized GNSS spoofing; maritime incidents in Eastern Mediterranean, Black Sea, and Persian Gulf. Starlink and VSAT interception research is active. Classified as #5 because the attacker sits between legitimate endpoints and manipulates the signal path.

references.title: C4ADS — Above Us Only Stars (GNSS spoofing)

instances.notes: Viasat KA-SAT 2022 is the canonical case: the AcidRain wiper entered via the ground-segment management network and propagated to customer modems as trusted firmware. Textbook #10 with the TAE at the modem firmware acceptance.

Intentional RF interference against commercial Satcom (Starlink, ViaSat, Inmarsat) documented in Russia/Ukraine and Iran/Israel theaters. Uplink flooding saturates the shared spectrum — classified as #6 at the RF layer.

references.title: ITU Radio Regulations Board RFI reports
